requirements.quote:
*  The ":path" pseudo-header field includes the path and query parts
      of the target URI (the absolute-path production and, optionally, a
      '?' character followed by the query production; see Section 4.1 of
      [HTTP]).  A request in asterisk form (for OPTIONS) includes the
      value '*' for the ":path" pseudo-header field.
requirements.condition: When encoding the ":path" pseudo-header field for a request other than the stated asterisk-form case.
requirements.required_behavior: Include the target URI path and, when present, its query component in ":path".
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not include URI components outside the path and optional query.
requirements.why_checkable: The value of ":path" can be compared with the path and query components of the target URI.

requirements.quote:
*  The ":path" pseudo-header field includes the path and query parts
      of the target URI (the absolute-path production and, optionally, a
      '?' character followed by the query production; see Section 4.1 of
      [HTTP]).  A request in asterisk form (for OPTIONS) includes the
      value '*' for the ":path" pseudo-header field.
requirements.condition: When an OPTIONS request uses asterisk form.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the ":path" pseudo-header field value to '*'.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can inspect the ":path" value of an asterisk-form OPTIONS request.

requirements.quote:
This pseudo-header field MUST NOT be empty for "http" or "https"
      URIs; "http" or "https" URIs that do not contain a path component
      MUST include a value of '/'.  The exceptions to this rule are:
requirements.condition: For an "http" or "https" URI, subject to the listed OPTIONS and CONNECT exceptions.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The ":path" pseudo-header field must not be empty.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation test can inspect whether ":path" is empty for an HTTP or HTTPS URI.

requirements.quote:
This pseudo-header field MUST NOT be empty for "http" or "https"
      URIs; "http" or "https" URIs that do not contain a path component
      MUST include a value of '/'.  The exceptions to this rule are:
requirements.condition: For an "http" or "https" URI with no path component, subject to the listed OPTIONS and CONNECT exceptions.
requirements.required_behavior: Include a ":path" value of '/'.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can construct a URI without a path component and inspect the encoded ":path" value.

requirements.quote:
-  an OPTIONS request for an "http" or "https" URI that does not
         include a path component; these MUST include a ":path" pseudo-
         header field with a value of '*' (see Section 7.1 of [HTTP]).
requirements.condition: For an OPTIONS request targeting an "http" or "https" URI without a path component.
requirements.required_behavior: Include a ":path" pseudo-header field whose value is '*'.
requirements.why_checkable: The request method, URI path presence, pseudo-header presence, and exact value are observable.

requirements.quote:
-  CONNECT requests (Section 8.5), where the ":path" pseudo-header
         field is omitted.
requirements.condition: For a CONNECT request.
requirements.required_behavior: Omit the ":path" pseudo-header field.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not include the ":path" pseudo-header field.
requirements.why_checkable: A CONNECT request's header block can be inspected for absence of ":path".

requirements.quote:
All HTTP/2 requests MUST include exactly one valid value for the
   ":method", ":scheme", and ":path" pseudo-header fields, unless they
   are CONNECT requests (Section 8.5).  An HTTP request that omits
   mandatory pseudo-header fields is malformed (Section 8.1.1).
requirements.condition: For an HTTP/2 request that is not a CONNECT request.
requirements.required_behavior: Include exactly one valid ":method" pseudo-header field value.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not omit or duplicate ":method", and do not supply an invalid value.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat omission of this mandatory pseudo-header field as a malformed request.
requirements.why_checkable: A decoded request header block can be checked for the count and validity of ":method" and for malformed-request handling.

requirements.quote:
All HTTP/2 requests MUST include exactly one valid value for the

requirements.condition: For an HTTP/2 request that is not a CONNECT request.
requirements.required_behavior: Include exactly one valid ":scheme" pseudo-header field value.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not omit or duplicate ":scheme", and do not supply an invalid value.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat omission of this mandatory pseudo-header field as a malformed request.
requirements.why_checkable: A decoded request header block can be checked for the count and validity of ":scheme" and for malformed-request handling.

requirements.quote:
All HTTP/2 requests MUST include exactly one valid value for the

requirements.condition: For an HTTP/2 request that is not a CONNECT request.
requirements.required_behavior: Include exactly one valid ":path" pseudo-header field value.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not omit or duplicate ":path", and do not supply an invalid value.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat omission of this mandatory pseudo-header field as a malformed request.
requirements.why_checkable: A decoded request header block can be checked for the count and validity of ":path" and for malformed-request handling.

requirements.quote:
Individual HTTP/2 requests do not carry an explicit indicator of
   protocol version.  All HTTP/2 requests implicitly have a protocol
   version of "2.0" (see Section 6.2 of [HTTP]).
requirements.condition: For every HTTP/2 request.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent its protocol version implicitly as "2.0".
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not carry an explicit protocol-version indicator in the individual request.
requirements.why_checkable: A request representation can be checked for absence of an explicit version indicator and for the implementation-assigned version value.

requirements.quote:
For HTTP/2 responses, a single ":status" pseudo-header field is
   defined that carries the HTTP status code field (see Section 15 of
   [HTTP]).  This pseudo-header field MUST be included in all responses,
   including interim responses; otherwise, the response is malformed
   (Section 8.1.1).
requirements.condition: For every HTTP/2 response, including an interim response.
requirements.required_behavior: Include the ":status" pseudo-header field carrying the HTTP status code.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat a response without ":status" as malformed.
requirements.why_checkable: Response header blocks, including interim ones, can be inspected for ":status" and omission handling.

requirements.quote: HTTP/2 responses implicitly have a protocol version of "2.0".
requirements.condition: For every HTTP/2 response.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent its protocol version implicitly as "2.0".
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's decoded response metadata can be checked for the implicit version value.

requirements.quote:
A client can request that server push be disabled, though this is
   negotiated for each hop independently.  The SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH
   setting can be set to 0 to indicate that server push is disabled.
requirements.condition: When SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH is set to 0 on a hop.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret the setting as indicating that server push is disabled for that hop.
requirements.why_checkable: A peer's push behavior and setting interpretation can be tested after receiving SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH value 0.

requirements.quote:
Promised requests MUST be safe (see Section 9.2.1 of [HTTP]) and
   cacheable (see Section 9.2.3 of [HTTP]).  Promised requests cannot
   include any content or a trailer section.  Clients that receive a
   promised request that is not cacheable, that is not known to be safe,
   or that indicates the presence of request content MUST reset the
   promised stream with a stream error (Section 5.4.2) of type
   PROTOCOL_ERROR.  Note that this could result in the promised stream
   being reset if the client does not recognize a newly defined method
   as being safe.
requirements.condition: For every promised request.
requirements.required_behavior: The promised request must use a method known to be safe.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not promise a request that is not known to be safe.
requirements.error_behavior: A client receiving such a promised request must reset the promised stream with a stream error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A promised request's method classification and the client's resulting stream reset and error code are observable.

requirements.quote:
Promised requests MUST be safe (see Section 9.2.1 of [HTTP]) and
   cacheable (see Section 9.2.3 of [HTTP]).  Promised requests cannot
   include any content or a trailer section.  Clients that receive a
   promised request that is not cacheable, that is not known to be safe,
   or that indicates the presence of request content MUST reset the
   promised stream with a stream error (Section 5.4.2) of type
   PROTOCOL_ERROR.  Note that this could result in the promised stream
   being reset if the client does not recognize a newly defined method
   as being safe.
requirements.condition: For every promised request.
requirements.required_behavior: The promised request must be cacheable.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not promise a request that is not cacheable.
requirements.error_behavior: A client receiving such a promised request must reset the promised stream with a stream error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: Request cacheability and the client's resulting stream reset and error code can be tested.

requirements.quote:
Promised requests MUST be safe (see Section 9.2.1 of [HTTP]) and
   cacheable (see Section 9.2.3 of [HTTP]).  Promised requests cannot
   include any content or a trailer section.  Clients that receive a
   promised request that is not cacheable, that is not known to be safe,
   or that indicates the presence of request content MUST reset the
   promised stream with a stream error (Section 5.4.2) of type
   PROTOCOL_ERROR.  Note that this could result in the promised stream
   being reset if the client does not recognize a newly defined method

requirements.condition: For every promised request.
requirements.error_behavior: A client receiving a promised request that indicates the presence of request content must reset the promised stream with a stream error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A promised request can be constructed with an indication of content and the emitted stream reset can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
Promised requests MUST be safe (see Section 9.2.1 of [HTTP]) and
   cacheable (see Section 9.2.3 of [HTTP]).  Promised requests cannot
   include any content or a trailer section.  Clients that receive a
   promised request that is not cacheable, that is not known to be safe,
   or that indicates the presence of request content MUST reset the
   promised stream with a stream error (Section 5.4.2) of type
   PROTOCOL_ERROR.  Note that this could result in the promised stream
   being reset if the client does not recognize a newly defined method
   as being safe.
requirements.condition: For every promised request.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not include a trailer section.
requirements.why_checkable: The promised request representation can be inspected for a trailer section.

requirements.quote:
Pushed responses that are cacheable (see Section 3 of [CACHING]) can
   be stored by the client, if it implements an HTTP cache.  Pushed
   responses are considered successfully validated on the origin server
   (e.g., if the "no-cache" cache response directive is present; see
   Section 5.2.2.4 of [CACHING]) while the stream identified by the
   promised stream identifier is still open.
requirements.condition: When a pushed response is cacheable and the client implements an HTTP cache.
requirements.required_behavior: The client may store the pushed response.
requirements.why_checkable: Cache contents can be inspected after receipt of a cacheable pushed response.

requirements.quote:
Pushed responses that are cacheable (see Section 3 of [CACHING]) can
   be stored by the client, if it implements an HTTP cache.  Pushed
   responses are considered successfully validated on the origin server
   (e.g., if the "no-cache" cache response directive is present; see
   Section 5.2.2.4 of [CACHING]) while the stream identified by the
   promised stream identifier is still open.
requirements.condition: While the stream identified by the promised stream identifier remains open.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the pushed response as successfully validated on the origin server.
requirements.why_checkable: Cache validation state can be observed while the associated promised stream is open.

requirements.quote:
Pushed responses that are not cacheable MUST NOT be stored by any
   HTTP cache.  They MAY be made available to the application
   separately.
requirements.condition: When a pushed response is not cacheable.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not store the pushed response in any HTTP cache.
requirements.why_checkable: Cache state can be inspected after receipt of a non-cacheable pushed response.

requirements.quote:
Pushed responses that are not cacheable MUST NOT be stored by any
   HTTP cache.  They MAY be made available to the application
   separately.
requirements.condition: When a pushed response is not cacheable.
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation may make the response available separately to the application.
requirements.why_checkable: The application-facing delivery path can be observed independently of HTTP-cache storage.

requirements.quote:
The server MUST include a value in the ":authority" pseudo-header
   field for which the server is authoritative (see Section 10.1).  A
   client MUST treat a PUSH_PROMISE for which the server is not
   authoritative as a stream error (Section 5.4.2) of type
   PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When a server sends a PUSH_PROMISE.
requirements.required_behavior: Include a ":authority" pseudo-header value for an authority for which the server is authoritative.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use an authority for which the server is not authoritative.
requirements.why_checkable: The promised authority can be compared with the server's configured or established authority set.

requirements.quote:
The server MUST include a value in the ":authority" pseudo-header
   field for which the server is authoritative (see Section 10.1).  A
   client MUST treat a PUSH_PROMISE for which the server is not
   authoritative as a stream error (Section 5.4.2) of type
   PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When a client receives a PUSH_PROMISE for an authority for which the server is not authoritative.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the PUSH_PROMISE as a stream error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A PUSH_PROMISE with an unauthorized authority can be injected and the error scope and code inspected.

requirements.quote:
A client cannot push.  Thus, servers MUST treat the receipt of a
   PUSH_PROMISE frame as a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type
   PROTOCOL_ERROR.  A server cannot set the SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH setting
   to a value other than 0 (see Section 6.5.2).
requirements.condition: When a server receives a PUSH_PROMISE frame from a client.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat receipt as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A client-originated PUSH_PROMISE can be sent and the server's connection-level error and code observed.

requirements.quote:
A client cannot push.  Thus, servers MUST treat the receipt of a
   PUSH_PROMISE frame as a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type
   PROTOCOL_ERROR.  A server cannot set the SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH setting
   to a value other than 0 (see Section 6.5.2).
requirements.condition: When a server sends the SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH setting.
requirements.required_behavior: Set SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH to 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not set SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH to any value other than 0.
requirements.why_checkable: The value in a server-sent SETTINGS frame can be inspected directly.

requirements.quote:
Server push is semantically equivalent to a server responding to a
   request; however, in this case, that request is also sent by the
   server, as a PUSH_PROMISE frame.
requirements.condition: When a server initiates server push.
requirements.required_behavior: Send the attributed request as a PUSH_PROMISE frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The frame sequence for a server push can be inspected for a PUSH_PROMISE carrying the request.

requirements.quote:
The PUSH_PROMISE frame includes a field block that contains control
   data and a complete set of request header fields that the server
   attributes to the request.  It is not possible to push a response to
   a request that includes message content.
requirements.condition: For every PUSH_PROMISE frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Include a field block containing control data and a complete set of request header fields attributed to the promised request.
requirements.why_checkable: A decoded PUSH_PROMISE field block can be checked for its control data and complete request header set.

requirements.quote:
The PUSH_PROMISE frame includes a field block that contains control
   data and a complete set of request header fields that the server
   attributes to the request.  It is not possible to push a response to
   a request that includes message content.
requirements.condition: When the associated request includes message content.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not push a response to that request.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can attempt server push for a request containing message content and observe whether a pushed response is produced.

requirements.quote:
Promised requests are always associated with an explicit request from
   the client.  The PUSH_PROMISE frames sent by the server are sent on
   that explicit request's stream.  The PUSH_PROMISE frame also includes
   a promised stream identifier, chosen from the stream identifiers
   available to the server (see Section 5.1.1).
requirements.condition: For every promised request.
requirements.required_behavior: Associate the promised request with an explicit client request.
requirements.why_checkable: The promised request can be traced to the client-initiated request stream on which its PUSH_PROMISE appears.

requirements.quote:
Promised requests are always associated with an explicit request from
   the client.  The PUSH_PROMISE frames sent by the server are sent on
   that explicit request's stream.  The PUSH_PROMISE frame also includes
   a promised stream identifier, chosen from the stream identifiers
   available to the server (see Section 5.1.1).
requirements.condition: When a server sends a PUSH_PROMISE associated with an explicit client request.
requirements.required_behavior: Send the PUSH_PROMISE on that explicit request's stream.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send it on an unrelated stream.
requirements.why_checkable: The stream carrying the PUSH_PROMISE can be compared with the associated client request stream.

requirements.quote:
Promised requests are always associated with an explicit request from
   the client.  The PUSH_PROMISE frames sent by the server are sent on
   that explicit request's stream.  The PUSH_PROMISE frame also includes
   a promised stream identifier, chosen from the stream identifiers
   available to the server (see Section 5.1.1).
requirements.condition: For every PUSH_PROMISE frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Include a promised stream identifier selected from the stream identifiers available to the server.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not select a stream identifier unavailable to the server.
requirements.why_checkable: The frame's promised stream identifier can be decoded and checked against the server's available identifier space.
